text.content:
Classification: Bloodline (African)

Called the Sphinxes by outsiders, the Laibon are believed by European Cainites to descend from vampires who migrated to Africa before the Sahara's spread cut the continent off from the rest of the world; the Laibon themselves believe they descend from the spirits of the land. Their kinship with animal spirits — especially great predators — gives them unusual mastery over their inner Beast. Laibon are intensely territorial and rarely interact with one another once a childe leaves her sire's home, communicating mainly through intermediaries on matters important to the bloodline as a whole. Islamic vampires expanding along trade routes into African kingdoms have begun clashing with Laibon territory, and traveling Laibon neonates now carry warnings and messages (backed by violence) alongside their traditional stories.

Disciplines: Animalism, Abombwe, Fortitude

Advantage: Laibon are the vampires of Africa (the Guruhi and their kin), often given free passage in Europe as curiosities uninterested in the War of Princes.

Disadvantage: Control over the Beast costs blood: each time a Laibon uses or consumes blood, the Beast consumes an extra Trait (or two, if the change in blood pool is five or more Traits in a single scene).

Organization: Solitary and territorial, each keeping to their own domain; young Laibon undertake extensive travel as a rite of passage before claiming domains of their own.

Suggested Viae: Beast and Heaven, with cultural variation.
